chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Zayd Abī al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abī Nuʿaym, who said:

I came to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) while he was in al-Madīnah, and I said to him: Upon me is a vow between al-Rukn and al-Maqām that, if I meet you, I will not leave al-Madīnah until I know whether you are the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or not. But he did not answer me with anything.

So I stayed for thirty days. Then he met me on a road and said: O Ḥakam, are you still here? I said: Yes, I informed you of what I had made binding upon myself for Allah, but you neither instructed me nor forbade me regarding anything, and you did not answer me with anything. He said: Come to me early tomorrow morning at the house. So I went to him in the morning, and he (عليه السلام) said: Ask about your need.

So I said: I made binding upon myself for Allah a vow, fasting, and charity between al-Rukn and al-Maqām that, if I were to meet you, I would not leave al-Madīnah until I knew whether you are the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or not. If it is you, I will remain attached to you; and if it is not you, I will travel through the land and seek livelihood.

He said: O Ḥakam, all of us are Qāʾim by the command of Allah. I said: Then are you al-Mahdī? He said: All of us guide to Allah. I said: Then are you the صاحب السيف, the possessor of the sword? He said: All of us are possessors of the sword and inheritors of the sword. I said: Then are you the one who will kill the enemies of Allah, through whom the friends of Allah will be strengthened, and through whom the religion of Allah will become manifest?

He said: O Ḥakam, how could I be that one when I have reached forty-five years of age, while the صاحب هذا الأمر, the master of this affair, is more recently acquainted with milk than I am and lighter upon the back of a riding animal?

key_terms.الرُّكْنِ وَالْمَقَامِ: the sacred location near the Kaʿbah used here to emphasize the solemnity of the vow
key_terms.النَّذْرُ: a binding vow made for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْمَعَاشَ: livelihood or means of worldly sustenance
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: the divinely guided one awaited at the end of time
key_terms.صَاحِبَ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the master of this divinely ordained affair, referring here to the awaited final Imam
key_terms.صَاحِبُ السَّيْفِ: the one associated with armed uprising and decisive establishment of truth
key_terms.قَائِمُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the awaited one from the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم who rises with divine authority

ai.seo_question: Are all the Imams called Qāʾim, or is that title only for the awaited Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about whether he was the awaited Qāʾim from the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. The Imam explains that all the Imams are qāʾim by the command of Allah and all guide to Him, while distinguishing the specific eschatological figure of the final صاحب هذا الأمر from himself. The report highlights both the shared authority of the Imams and the distinct identity of the awaited Mahdi.
